plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up goblet-shaped pinkish-lilac flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-like leaves appear the following spring and die back by summer. All parts are highly toxic due to colchicine.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to Europe from Ireland to the Balkans; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Asia
plants.funFact: Because flowers appear without leaves, it is nicknamed 'naked ladies'. Colchicine from this plant is used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce polyploidy.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust North American wildflower that forms dense clumps topped with masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It thrives in meadows, roadsides, and wet prairies and is a crucial late-season nectar source.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Canada to Alabama; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Migrating monarch butterflies depend heavily on its nectar to fuel their long journey to Mexico around the autumn equinox.

plants.name: Prunus campanulata
plants.description: Not typical for this date in the north, but in the Southern Hemisphere's spring, many flowering trees such as Jacaranda mimosifolia begin to bloom. Jacaranda is a tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves and clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers that carpet streets.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (September to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Jacaranda blooms in Pretoria, South Africa, are so famous that the city is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City'. Note: the scientific name for this entry is Jacaranda mimosifolia, not Prunus campanulata.

plants.name: Lycoris radiata
plants.description: A striking bulbous perennial with spidery, bright red flowers with long curved stamens that emerge on bare stalks in early autumn. Leaves appear after the flowers fade and persist through winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Native to China, Korea and Japan; naturalized in the southeastern United States
plants.funFact: In Japan it is called higanbana, since it blooms around the autumn equinox holiday of Higan, and is often seen along rice paddies and cemeteries.
